look_here_first: Start with growth form and the short flowering shoots: creek plum is a clonal, thicket-forming shrub with alternate simple serrate leaves, small white flower clusters on short shoots, and rounded single-stoned plum fruits. Check leaf-margin glands when present, but do not require them on older leaves because they can be shed.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: reviewed UT local treatment describes shoots as not spinescent; do not teach universal thorniness

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Alternate, simple and serrate; glands may occur near the margin but absence on mature leaves is not decisive.

key_traits.label: Flower
key_traits.text: Small white Prunus flowers clustered on short shoots; confirm the plum/cherry floral plan rather than relying on color.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Rounded plum-like drupe containing one stone.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Usually a clonal thicket-forming shrub rather than the small-tree habit typical of Mexican plum.
